zones.label: Column 1 running header
zones.note: Lexical aid: Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, version 202510 (supplied page subset), CC BY 4.0. https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html ; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . Used for lexical identification after reading the scan, not as the authority for diplomatic spelling or typography. Lexical references are paraphrased in the English comments; the transcription was read independently from this scan.

lines.note: Continues the armour example from f0441: he armed himself completely. Armouſe is running text here, whereas its repetition at the previous page's foot is the catchword; embranco retains the printed spacing.
Sashikazashi means carrying something raised in front of oneself. The abbreviated bã- starts bandeira, a flag, across the line ending.

runs.text: deira, ou algũa couſa diante na mão. Vt,

lines.note: Completes bandeira and adds another object held out in the hand. Ca- begins the sword example, not an abbreviation in the Portuguese apparatus.
Katana wo makkoo ni sashikazaite kakaru describes advancing with the sword raised in front. Sashikazaite is a historical inflection; Le- starts the Portuguese translation.

runs.text: uando a Catana feita, ou aleuantada diante do

lines.note: Completes Leuando: carrying the sword set or raised in front of the face. Catana occurs within the Portuguese explanation and is therefore a typeface-toggle candidate.
Completes the forward-rush example. Oogi wo sashikazasu then illustrates the same action with a folding fan rather than a sword.

runs.text: Aleuantar o abano diante na mão.

lines.note: The fan is raised in front in the hand. Abano is the Portuguese object and the entire row is the translation of the preceding Japanese example.
Sashichigaye describes two people killing each other. En- begins entre, and the manner of the killing is specified on the next row.

runs.text: tre ſi às punhaladas, ou estocadas.

lines.note: Completes entre si: the two kill each other with dagger blows or sword thrusts. The mark in às is an accent, not the draft's nasal tilde.
Sashikoroshi means killing by stabbing or thrusting. Oita is the printed historical past-part abbreviation and is not modernized to oshita.
Adds dagger blows as the alternative manner of killing. This is the continuation of the preceding verb's gloss.
Sashikoye means passing over or ahead of someone. Di- begins diante on the next line; the following examples distinguish physical and social senses.
Completes 'ahead of someone'. Hito wo sashikoyuru illustrates passing over a person, with Paſ- beginning the Portuguese verb across the break.

runs.text: ſar, ou ſaltar por cima dalguem. ¶

lines.note: The first example means passing or jumping over someone. Saxi- starts a second example applying the verb to speaking over another person's position.
Sashikoyete yuu means speaking without acknowledging or deferring to someone. The translation continues its description of the disregarded person below.

runs.text: ter deuer com algũa peßoa a quẽſe deuia de ter

lines.note: The person ought to receive due consideration. The visible noun is peßoa, correcting peßa; the abbreviated quẽ and close ſe attachment are retained.
Respect completes the explanation of speaking without proper deference. This closes the social sense of sashikoyete yuu.
Sashikube means putting firewood into the fire. Lenha is visible rather than the draft's lenba, and the gloss directly confirms the Japanese action.
Sashikudashi means sending something down from a superior position. Reca- starts recado, a message, in a list that also includes people.

runs.text: do, ou gente, &c. de lugar alto, ou ſuperi-

lines.note: Completes recado and specifies sending a message or people from a high or superior place. The damaged last letter of lugar is read as r, not e.

runs.text: or. ¶ Item, Abaixar algũa couſa de riba.

lines.note: Completes superior and adds the literal sense of lowering something from above. De riba is the historical Portuguese expression retained here.
Nawa wo sashikudasu means lowering a rope. The paragraph sign is visible before the example and was omitted in the draft.
Completes 'put the rope down'. The two-word continuation remains a body line, not a separate lexical item.
Sashikuwae means adding something to something else. The historical spelling Acrecentar and the visible cou- line division are preserved.
Completes the addition gloss. Ninju wo sashikuwayuru means adding more people; the Japanese verb is divided before ru.
Completes sashikuwayuru and translates it as increasing the number of people. The historical yuru form is not replaced by modern eru.

runs.text: Hũa maneira de caixa, ou caixão q̃

lines.note: Sashidaru is described as a kind of box or chest. The scan reads maneira, not manetra; q̃ introduces its usual finish below.
The container is ordinarily lacquered. Vruxado is the Portuguese predicate printed here, reflecting the urushi-related coating rather than a separate Japanese example.
This nominal sashidashi is a register of the local cultivators. It is not the later verbal sashidashi entry describing extending something outward.
Sashide means coming forward without being called. The scan reads Sair, correcting Sar; zzuru preserves the historical voiced consonant notation.
The proverb says that coming forward is half of learning. Iy tçutayeta presents it as a transmitted saying; the Portuguese explanation follows rather than another headword.

runs.text: Dizem ordinariamente que o ſer deſpejado, &

lines.note: The saying is commonly understood as praising being bold or forthcoming. The damaged but recoverable word is ordinariamente, not the draft's separated o dinariamente.

runs.text: entremetido he meo caminho andado, pera eſ-

lines.note: Being forward is said to be half the journey already made toward learning. Meo retains its historical spelling, and eſ- begins eſtudar.

runs.text: tudar, ou pera aprender qual quer outra arte.

lines.note: Completes eſtudar and extends the saying to learning any other art. The visible phrase qual quer is retained with its printed separation, correcting qual juer.
Sashideta hito, alternatively sashide, denotes an intrusive or forward person. The missing paragraph sign is restored; Homẽ keeps its abbreviation tilde.
Completes entremetido and introduces sashide wo yuu, speaking intrusively or presumptuously. The Portuguese manner adverb continues below.
Completes the description of intrusive and rash speech. The historical adverb arremeſadamente is preserved as printed rather than replaced by a modern synonym.
Sashihage means having an arrow fitted or nocked to the bow. The close aſeta spelling is retained; the object arco follows below.
Completes 'in the bow' and gives ya wo sashihaguru, nocking the arrow. This example confirms the archery sense rather than the unrelated modern word hageru.
Sashihanashi means releasing or letting something go from oneself. The definition continues directly with si below.
Inu wo sashihanaite yaru illustrates letting a dog loose. The historical hanaite inflection agrees with the headword's aita and is not regularized to hanashite.

runs.text: o cão, & deixalo ir por onde quer.

lines.note: The dog is released and allowed to go wherever it wants. This completes the example rather than adding another verb sense.
Sashihasami means pinching, pressing, or placing something between other things. The headword's f and long s belong to distinct sounds and are retained.

runs.text: pertar algũa couſa com outra de maneira que

lines.note: Completes apertar: pressing one thing with another so that it stays crosswise or caught between them. The result follows on the next row.
The example concerns the side or edge of ookuchi trousers. It illustrates tucking clothing into the belt; Vôcuchino keeps the printed circumflex.

runs.text: Meter aborda de hũs certos cal-

lines.note: Completes the tucking action. The Portuguese describes the edge of a particular kind of trousers; aborda retains its close spacing and cal- continues below.

runs.text: ções que ſeruem nos autos na cinta. ¶ Per

lines.note: The trousers are used in theatrical performances and their edge is tucked into the belt. The scan reads ções, not çõus; the restored paragraph sign introduces Per met., split across the columns.
Per met. marks a metaphorical extension across the column break. Ikon wo sashihasamu means harbouring resentment; the Portuguese reads no, not na, before coração.
Completes 'having hatred in the heart'. This closes the figurative extension of sashihasamu rather than introducing a new entry.
Sashihiki is equated with kakehiki and initially explained as attacking and withdrawing. The military object follows on the next row.
Completes attacking enemies and retreating. Shio no sashi-hiki then introduces the rising and falling of the tide.
Completes sashihiki, glossed as flood and ebb of the tide. The final accent in marè is retained from the scan.
Sanyoo no sashihiki applies the same contrast to accounting. The Portuguese deſ- begins deſcontar, deduction or subtraction.

runs.text: contar quando ſe fazem as contas.

lines.note: Completes deſcontar and explains adding and deducting while making accounts. Contas is Portuguese here, not Japanese source text.
Sashifusagi means blocking or obstructing. The principal forms use historical fusagu and fusaida without modernization.
The example describes enemy forces blocking the various roads. The final abbreviation is &c., not the draft's &e.; michimichi is the repeated road noun.

runs.text: Os inimigos impedindo, & tapando os ca-

lines.note: The Portuguese confirms that enemies are obstructing and blocking the roads. Ca- starts caminhos across the line break.
Completes caminhos, the roads blocked in the example. The short physical continuation is retained with its own ID.
Sashigatana is a katana or Japanese sword. Catana is embedded in the Portuguese definition, while Iapão is the Portuguese country name rather than a Japanese font-toggle term.
Sashigaye is a spare sword. Catana is embedded in Portuguese, and the historical spelling ſobreſelente is retained rather than modernized.
Sashigusuri is first an eye medicine. The worn right-edge abbreviation is read as Itẽ, introducing another sense; it is not the draft's It-. fragment.

runs.text: No Ximo mezinha pera botar a criança im-

lines.note: The dictionary gives a regional Ximo sense for a preparation said to expel a fetus. This records the historical lexical claim, not medical guidance; im- continues below.
Completes imperfeita and the description of expulsion from the womb. The source's historical wording is retained without treating it as a modern clinical classification.
Sashiidashi means extending or putting something out. The scan shows the extra i missing from Saxidaxi; fo continues as fora, without adding an unestablished line-end hyphen.
Completes fora and gives a hand or head as examples. Nusubito begins a proverb involving the mention of a thief.

Nusubito to iyeba te sashi idasu is a proverb about reacting defensively when a thief is mentioned. Reinspection retains the F-shaped initial in Frouerb.; it may be a damaged P, but the label is not silently normalized from its meaning alone.

runs.text: do ladrão logo ſe està ali, ſe ſalua dizendo que

lines.note: Completes nomeando: when a thief is mentioned, someone present immediately tries to clear himself. The scan reads dizendo, not dezendo.
The defensive person says it is not him. Fune wo sashi idasu then supplies the literal example of pushing a boat out.

runs.text: a embarcação fora ao mar com a vara.

lines.note: The boat is pushed out to sea with a pole. This completes the physical example rather than continuing the thief proverb.
Sashiide means coming out or appearing, as the moon or sun does. The printed internal space and abbreviated lũa are preserved.
The example identifies the direction where the sun comes out as east. Figaxi- continues with to xire below; the repeated i in ſaxiizzuru is retained.

runs.text: Aparte donde ſae o ſol ſabei que he

lines.note: Completes 'know it as east'. The Portuguese says to recognize the sun's rising direction; he corrects be at the gutter, and Aparte retains its printed close spacing.
East completes the previous sentence. Oriente is Portuguese, and this single-word line is not a new Japanese entry.

Sashiiri means entering, as sunlight or brightness enters. The divided Portuguese word is claridade, read clarida- rather than claridu-; its last vowel is compressed at the gutter. The draft's terminal hyphen is retained where the impression is weak, and the printed Japanese space is preserved.
Completes claridade and gives hi ga mado e sashiiru, sunlight entering through a window. The final O begins the Portuguese sentence on the next row.
The sun enters through the window. Pella and janella retain the historical doubled consonants of the printed Portuguese.

Sashimakase means entrusting or handing something over. Cou- begins couſa below, with c correcting the draft's t. The last letters are compressed at the gutter; the supplied terminal hyphen is retained rather than treated as newly established from the word division alone.

runs.text: ſa a outro, ou deixala à ſua vontade.

lines.note: Completes couſa and explains leaving it to another person's discretion. Vontade corrects the draft's voniade and is supported by the visible t.
Sashimaneki means beckoning or signalling with the hand. The gutter does not erase the full mão or its following comma; the malformed mo is corrected.
The example raises a fan and signals toward the open sea. Catauo retains its final o at the gutter, correcting the incomplete catau.
Completes the signalling action and starts 'raising the fan'. The visible abano and comma replace the draft's abam.

runs.text: & acenando là pera o largo, ou alto do mar.

lines.note: The signalling is directed out toward the open or high sea. The grave accent in là is preserved rather than replaced with a modern acute.
Sashimawari describes moving around while stinging. The gutter abbreviation is Vt, introducing an example, not the draft's Vi.
Hachi ga koko kashiko wo sashimawaru describes bees moving here and there while stinging. The Portuguese plural article As is visible at the gutter, not merely a.

runs.text: abelhas rodeão picando por diuerſas partes.

lines.note: The bees fly around stinging in different places. Abelhas corrects abeihas; the plural subject agrees with the restored As above.
Sashimawashi is the transitive counterpart, causing something to go around. The dictionary gives only this short gloss here.

runs.text: Certa iguaria de peixe crù que ſe co-

lines.note: Sashimi is described as a preparation of raw fish. The scan preserves crù with a grave; co- begins the verb come below.
The fish is eaten with a particular sauce. The historical definition does not name that sauce, so none is supplied.
Sashimo is labelled an adverb meaning 'so much' or 'to that extent'. The example begins with a visibly divided Sa- at the gutter.

runs.text: ximo cǒ aru Tçuguinobumo qimeno ta-

lines.note: The example concerns even so valiant a Tsuginobu being struck through the vital organs. The worn sequence is provisionally read qimeno; expected kimo no is a linguistic comparator, not grounds to normalize the visible vowel.
Completes tabane wo itoosare, being shot through the vital centre. The Portuguese trespaßa- starts the equivalent passive expression across the break.

runs.text: do o coração com hũa ſeta a Tçuguinobu tam

lines.note: The translation says that an arrow pierced the heart of the valiant Tsuginobu. Tam corrects the draft's tar; Tçuguinobu is a Japanese name embedded in Portuguese.
Valente completes tam valente, 'so valiant'. This closes the example illustrating the degree adverb sashimo.
Sashimoni is another adverbial form with the same meaning. The worn n is retained as n in the headword; Idem refers to the preceding sashimo entry.

zones.label: Printed catchword
zones.note: The small raised mark after Saximo is provisionally transcribed as a continuation hyphen. Its compressed impression near the gutter is not fully distinct; the catchword itself is roman, not display type.
